extracted.intended_audience: eligible hospitals and critical access hospitals (CAHs), health IT developers, payers, and other stakeholders commenting on the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program
extracted.subtask_short: Medicare PI HIE and ePA measures
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of proposed rule criteria for the Health Information Exchange objective and the Electronic Prior Authorization measure in the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program, including measure text, exclusions, certification requirements, scoring, timing, and transition provisions. Intended to guide eligible hospitals/CAHs, health IT developers, payers, and commenters on proposed obligations and options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of Support Electronic Referral Loops measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to remove the Support Electronic Referral Loops by Sending Health Information and Support Electronic Referral Loops by Receiving and Reconciling Health Information measures beginning with the EHR reporting period in CY 2028.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: network-based exchange measures (HIE Bi-Directional Exchange and Enabling Exchange Under TEFCA) are seen as more comprehensive indicators of meaningful exchange than single-recipient C-CDA summary-of-care document transmission; removal would streamline reporting and reduce program complexity. Acknowledges CAHs and small/rural hospitals currently reporting the removed measures; proposes CY2028 effective date to allow time to plan, procure, configure, and validate new workflows. Invites comments on additional barriers small, rural hospitals, or CAHs may face in reporting HIE Bi-Directional Exchange or Enabling Exchange Under TEFCA. Notes removal also intended to encourage adoption of non-document-centric modalities (e.g., FHIR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Health Information Exchange objective reporting requirement (post-removal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following removal of the Referral Loops measures, eligible hospitals and CAHs would be required to satisfy the Health Information Exchange objective by reporting the HIE Bi-Directional Exchange measure or reporting the Enabling Exchange Under TEFCA measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring policy: attesting “Yes” to either the HIE Bi-Directional Exchange or Enabling Exchange Under TEFCA measure would result in a maximum score of 30 points. Eligible hospitals would also be required to meet the Electronic Prior Authorization measure requirement in the Health Information Exchange objective. Invites public comment on these proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Prior Authorization (ePA) measure — original adopted requirement and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Original measure text (finalized in 2024): 'For at least one hospital discharge and medical item or service (excluding drugs) ordered during the EHR reporting period, the prior authorization is requested electronically via a Prior Authorization Application Programming Interface (API) using data from CEHRT.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions finalized: (1) eligible hospital/CAH does not order any medical items/services (excluding drugs) requiring prior authorization during the EHR reporting period; (2) only orders items/services requiring prior authorization from a payer that does not offer an API that meets CMS's specified Prior Authorization API requirements during the applicable EHR reporting period. Only a 'Yes' attestation, or claiming an applicable exclusion, fulfills the measure. For CY2027 the measure was finalized as unscored, but a 'No' attestation would result in not meeting the measure, not meeting minimum program requirements, and being subject to a downward payment adjustment. The measurement approach required prior authorization be requested via Prior Authorization API using CEHRT (as originally stated 'using data from CEHRT').

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed updated ePA measure wording (CY2027 onward)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revised measure text: 'For at least one medical item or service (excluding drugs) ordered during a hospital encounter that occurs within the EHR reporting period, the prior authorization is requested electronically through a Prior Authorization API using CEHRT.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key changes: replaces 'discharge' with 'encounter' to clarify timing (may occur any time during hospital encounter), and revises 'using data from CEHRT' to 'using CEHRT' to align with certification requirements. The proposal does not modify previously finalized exclusion criteria. CMS requests comment on whether allowing attestation based on checking coverage requirements (regardless of whether that check results in a request/approval) would be useful, and whether to include drugs in the measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to use certified health IT (CEHRT) for ePA measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal that an electronic prior authorization must be requested using CEHRT to satisfy the Electronic Prior Authorization measure, and that CEHRT must be comprised of health IT certified to specific certification criteria in 45 CFR 170.315(g)(31),(32),(33).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: specifying certified health IT ensures standards-based capabilities to interact with Prior Authorization APIs established by impacted payers. The certification criteria are based on HL7 Da Vinci IGs and address different parts of the ePA workflow. Use of certified Health IT Modules is required such that the measure action can be completed using standards-based transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification criterion: provider prior authorization API—coverage requirements discovery (45 CFR 170.315(g)(31))
rubrics_metrics.description: Certification criterion enabling a health care provider to request information from payers about coverage requirements (based on HL7 FHIR Da Vinci—Coverage Requirements Discovery (CRD) IG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables a real-time query to a payer endpoint to determine whether prior authorization is required and what documentation is needed. Example scenario: query returns an approval or returns coverage criteria; in some cases receipt of an approval in response to a query may satisfy the measure without further submission. A Health IT Module certified to this criterion alone may be sufficient in some situations for an eligible hospital/CAH to attest 'Yes' to the measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification criterion: provider prior authorization API—documentation templates and rules (45 CFR 170.315(g)(32))
rubrics_metrics.description: Certification criterion providing a mechanism for clinicians and EHR users to retrieve and assemble payer-specific documentation templates and rules (based on HL7 FHIR Da Vinci—Documentation Templates and Rules (DTR) IG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports navigation and automatic assembly of required documentation according to payer requirements (e.g., embedded SMART on FHIR app fetching templates, auto-populating clinical data using CQL and FHIR queries). Useful when initial coverage discovery indicates additional information is required prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification criterion: provider prior authorization API—prior authorization support (45 CFR 170.315(g)(33))
rubrics_metrics.description: Certification criterion enabling submission of prior authorization requests and checking the status of previously submitted requests (based on HL7 FHIR Da Vinci—Prior Authorization Support (PAS) IG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables bundling the request and documentation into a FHIR bundle and submitting it via a FHIR RESTful interaction to the payer's prior authorization endpoint; supports secure, standards-based transmission and status checks; when complete information is provided, payers may adjudicate/approve in near real-time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in using combinations of certified Health IT Modules
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible hospitals and CAHs can successfully attest to the ePA measure using only those certified Health IT Modules necessary to complete the measure; they are not required to adopt additional certified modules that are not needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS expects different prior authorization scenarios will require different combinations of modules (CRD only vs. CRD+DTR+PAS). Examples provided show that a successful attestation may result from differing module configurations. This affords flexibility to hospitals, CAHs, and developers in deployment and adoption of certified functionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal to make the ePA measure an optional 10-point bonus for CY2027
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to make the Electronic Prior Authorization measure optional and eligible for 10 bonus points for eligible hospitals and CAHs that attest 'Yes' for the EHR reporting period in CY2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: allow additional time for procurement, integration, and testing; provide flexibility for small, rural, and under-resourced hospitals; address implementation complexity due to prior authorization API standards changes. Operational rules: exclusions would not be available for the optional bonus measure; only 'Yes' earns 10 bonus points; 'No' yields no bonus but does not cause the hospital/CAH to fail minimum program requirements or be considered not a meaningful EHR user for CY2027. CMS invites comment on this proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal to require the ePA measure beginning CY2028 (with exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal that eligible hospitals and CAHs would be required to attest 'Yes' to the updated Electronic Prior Authorization measure beginning with the EHR reporting period in CY2028, or claim an applicable exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only a 'Yes' attestation or claiming an applicable exclusion would fulfill the measure; a 'No' would result in not meeting the measure, not meeting minimum program requirements, not being considered a meaningful EHR user, and being subject to a downward payment adjustment. The previously adopted exclusions (did not order any relevant items/services; only ordered from payers without compliant APIs) would be available for CY2028 and subsequent years. CMS also proposes to keep the measure unscored for CY2028 and subsequent years to allow time for adjustment to the workflow without scoring implications, and invites comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration for future performance-based or expanded ePA measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for information on potential future updates to expand the measure beyond 'at least one' electronic prior authorization to incentivize broader and sustained use of electronic prior authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS envisions expanding scope in future rulemaking to increase interoperable exchange, reduce administrative burden, and improve timely access to services. They seek comment on how to strengthen the measure to incentivize progress while minimizing burden, and on barriers small, rural, or under-resourced hospitals/CAHs might face in reporting a performance-based ePA measure. Also requests comment on including drugs in the measure.
